messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> INC-78921: canary-probe eu-canary-auth-01 returning 5xx (503) > threshold 
PagerDuty: Incident INC-78921 created and paged rotation: SRE Oncall (details: https://pagerduty.example/INC78921) :rotating_light:
Alex W: ACKing oncall — taking initial lead, will triage
Maria G: pulling logs from eu-auth-01 now, seeing a sudden cluster of 503s starting ~T-40s
Jamal K: any recent deploys to auth in eu?
Alex W: I don't see any deploys in the last 6 hours for auth service in EU. no releases on the board.
Priya S: quick grep of probe runner -> looks like probe retry rate jumped, might be triggering cascades. attaching sample output:
```
[2026-03-15T12:02:05Z] eu-canary-auth-01 request_id=abc123 status=503 upstream=timeout
[2026-03-15T12:02:06Z] eu-canary-auth-01 request_id=abc124 status=503 upstream=502
```
Alex W: good call — could be probe amplification. are customer requests affected?
Maria G: checking prod metrics -> auth 5xx for user traffic is flat at ~0.02% but probe-specific metrics show 4.8% 503 on the canary probe host
Jamal K: ok so likely synthetic-only. still noisy pager because threshold was for global probe fanout. we should suppress pager and fix probe config
Priya S: can we temporarily MUTE the probe alert in PagerDuty for eu region?
Alex W: granting intent: I will create a PD maintenance window for the probe checks, 30m. @PagerDuty please start maintenance for service 'synth-probes-eu'
PagerDuty: Maintenance window created for service 'synth-probes-eu' (30 minutes) by Alex W
SRE Oncall: also recommending we scale down probe fanout to single probe to avoid amplifying upstream transient failures — will patch probe-runner config now
Maria G: I pushed a change to the probe config to reduce concurrent probes from 50 -> 5 and added exponential backoff (PR: https://git.example/r/probe-runner/pulls/402) :white_check_mark:
Priya S: running quick curl check against the auth endpoint from eu probe host:
```
curl -i https://auth.eu.example/health
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","uptime":87432}
```
Priya S: direct user-facing health looks fine, so synthetic-only failure confirmed
Alex W: note for incident log: no user reports, no increase in customer error rates, no crashloops. severity: pager noise / probe config & backoff bug.
Jamal K: can you add a one-off rule to circuit-break probe retries? will reduce spam on alerts.
SRE Oncall: added temporary rule to suppress repeated failures from single probe host for 10 minutes (config updated)
Maria G: collecting traces for 503s — they show connection resets from an intermediate LB (lb-eu-2) around the same time window
Alex W: contacting infra on-call to check LB health and recent config changes @infra-oncall
Priya S: infra responded: no config change, but LB saw transient spike in connection resets likely due to backend thread pool exhaustion — they are increasing pool size as mitigation
PagerDuty: User SRE Oncall acknowledged incident INC-78921
Incident-bot: escalation suppressed — maintenance window active.
Alex W: mitigation summary: 1) muted PD flapping by maintenance window 2) reduced probe fanout + backoff patch merged 3) temporary circuit-break suppression added 4) infra increased LB thread pool 5) monitoring: watch 15m
Maria G: post-change metrics -> probe 503 rate falling to 0.7% after 2 minutes, user-facing 5xx still stable
Jamal K: creating a follow-up ticket to harden probe-runner (ensure exponential backoff by default, increase jitter, and add rate limiter) -> TASK-1456
Priya S: capturing communications for postmortem: minimal customer impact, root-cause likely probe retry amplification + transient LB pressure. action items listed in TASK-1456 and ENG-SRE backlog.
Alex W: OK handing off to night SRE — @SRE Oncall you're the primary for the follow-up. I'll update PD incident with notes and close the temporary maintenance once we confirm stability
SRE Oncall: on it, will keep an eye for 30m and close if stable.
PagerDuty: Incident INC-78921 resolved (status: monitored -> resolved) by Alex W.
Alex W: closing thread — marking as resolved, will file short postmortem note tomorrow. :thumbsup:
